questions.question: What should this trial remote agent do?

options.label: Repo summary demo (Recommended)
options.description: Agent checks out ai-harness, reads the README + repo layout, and writes a short summary of what the project does. Read-only, harmless, easy to verify it ran.

options.label: Open-tickets digest
options.description: Agent runs `gh` to list open issues on the project boards and summarizes them. Needs gh auth in the remote env — may not be available.

options.label: Let me describe it
options.description: You'll tell me the exact task/prompt for the agent.

options.label: Once, in ~5 min (Recommended)
options.description: One-time run_once_at a few minutes from now, so you can watch it fire and then it auto-disables. Best for a trial.

options.label: Recurring
options.description: A cron schedule (minimum interval is 1 hour). I'll ask for the cadence.

questions.question: Which environment should it run in?

options.label: Anthropic cloud (Recommended)
options.description: env 'Family Fund' (anthropic_cloud) — fully cloud, doesn't depend on your macmini/macbook being awake. Cleanest for a trial.

options.label: macmini:ai-harness
options.description: Bridge env on your macmini tied to ai-harness. Runs on your actual machine — needs it awake/online.

options.label: macbook:dev
options.description: Bridge env on your MacBook Pro. Runs on that machine — needs it awake/online.

transcript_tail.text:
Yes — there are a few distinct mechanisms, depending on what kind of "session" you mean. Here's the honest breakdown of what I can actually trigger from here:

## 1. Remote Claude Code agents — yes, directly
I have a `RemoteTrigger` tool that calls the claude.ai remote-trigger API (the same thing the `/schedule` skill wraps). With it I can:
- **`create`** a scheduled routine (cron or one-time) that spins up a Claude Code agent in the cloud
- **`run`** an existing trigger immediately, on demand
- `list` / `get` / `update` them

These run server-side and show up on claude.ai — not on your machine. This is the cleanest "you trigger a Claude session" path.

## 2. Codex — no cloud trigger, only local resume
There's no remote-trigger equivalent for Codex. The way this repo starts Codex work is `remote_control/usage_limit` spawning a detached **`codex exec resume`** subprocess in the session's recorded cwd (`monitor.py:293`). That's *resuming* an existing rollout, not opening a brand-new session. I could launch `codex exec ...` via Bash to start a fresh local one, but that's the crude manual route.

## 3. What the repo already does autonomously (I don't hand-trigger these)
- **`supervisor.py`** spawns long-running `claude remote-control` servers for each dir in `active-dirs.txt` — a background service, not per-task.
- **`usage_limit/monitor.py`** auto-resumes sessions paused by usage limits: Claude via a POST resume event to the cloud session API (`attempt_resume`), Codex via the local `codex exec resume` above.

## 4. Sub-agents (within *this* session)
I can also spawn `Agent` sub-agents for parallel work — but those are children of this conversation, not standalone Claude Code/Codex sessions.

---

So: **remote Claude Code → yes, I can create or fire one now.** **Codex → only local spawn/resume via Bash.** 

Want me to actually do one — e.g. fire off a scheduled remote Claude routine, or list what triggers already exist?
Let me first see what triggers already exist, so we either reuse one or create a fresh simple one.
No triggers exist yet, so we'll create one. Let me check the `/schedule` skill for the exact body format the create call expects.
The `/schedule` skill is built-in (not file-based). Let me invoke it to get the correct body format and requirements.
Good — let's create one. A few quick choices, then I'll show you the full config before firing.
